title: Group eval is fed the real per-candidate recruiter breakdown + role band, carries one clear recommendation, and is decidable inline
expected: A side-by-side comparison on the SAME dimensions, a clear recommended lead with concrete why, that he can act on without recruiter work.
got: runGroupEval pulls each candidate's full deterministic recruiter breakdown (per-dim scores, confidence, matched/missing with provenance, fit tier), their own salary expectation, and a cached AI reasoning; the compare-all narrative gets real dims + role band, not labels alone. AI verdict shows a single boxed recommendation; Tomas can advance/reject the lead inline from the modal.
suggested_acceptance: Group eval shows a single clear recommended lead, the same dimensions for every candidate, and an inline accept/reject — no tagging or CV-reading required.

title: First group-eval generation is a cold background task behind a spinner
got: Eval is generated by a background task; per-candidate reasoning runs concurrently up to the cap of 6 but cold Python spawns are slow. Cached re-open is fast. First run could nibble his <15 min window, especially keyless/degraded.
l2_priority: Time a real cold generation end-to-end; confirm cached re-open is instant and the first run stays well inside 15 min.
suggested_acceptance: A first group-eval generation returns a usable comparison within a budget that leaves Tomas time to decide inside 15 minutes.

title: Interview prep questions are grounded in the candidate's real CV + the real role, with honest provenance and one-click copy
expected: Questions specific to THIS role that a seasoned manager would actually ask, handed to him, not assigned.
got: runInterviewPrep -> runAutomationTask('prep') serializes the candidate's full profile JSON to the prompt with the real --job-id and recruiter --lang; early-career entries get the student script. Source (llm/deterministic) is disclosed with an amber 'not tailored' note on fallback. Whole pack is copyable; human scorecard/notes survive a regenerate.
l2_priority: Generate a real prep pack and assert the questions name role/CV-specific detail (not generic filler) and the rubric is gradeable.
suggested_acceptance: Generated prep questions reference the candidate's actual CV and the specific role, with the source (AI vs template) clearly disclosed.

title: Prep lives under Schedule; the nav 'Interview sim' item is the voice sim, not prep — a slight intent mismatch for an occasional user
expected: An occasional manager looking for 'interview prep' finds it where he'd look.
got: Prep is reached from a candidate card in the Schedule tab ('Priprava na pohovor'); the sidebar 'Interview sim' item opens the voice interview simulator, not prep. An occasional user might check the Interview item first.
l2_priority: Confirm Tomas locates the prep button from the Schedule candidate card within ~5 seconds without a tutorial.
suggested_acceptance: From the Schedule candidate card, interview prep is reachable in one obvious click.

title: Offer-accept card has no on-page link to onboarding; reads as the 'we'll be in touch' dead-end the journey targets
expected: Accept on /offer/[token] lands on a concrete onboarding next-step (the pre-boarding questionnaire), not a dead-end thank-you.
got: The accepted state renders ONLY the body text acceptedBodyCompany/acceptedBodyGeneric, whose Czech is literally 'Nas personalni tym se vam brzy ozve s podrobnostmi k nastupu' (HR will be in touch). No link/button to /onboarding/[token] on the page; the onboarding link is delivered only via the async welcome comm. So a candidate accepting on-screen still hits a dead-end.
scope_note: This is the CANDIDATE surface (/offer/[token]) — Tereza's, not in Tomas's reachable set. Tagged unreachable for Tomas; his own offer-approval + onboarding-handoff legs pass. Defer the job-impact verdict to Tereza's L2.
l2_priority: On Tereza's L2: accept a real offer token and confirm the accepted state links onward to the minted onboarding questionnaire (or flag the missing link).
suggested_acceptance: After accepting on /offer/[token], the candidate sees an on-page link/button to their onboarding questionnaire, not only a 'we'll be in touch' message.

title: Internal offer approval is one grounded action: number, band position, rationale, and a single 'Accept & send offer' button
expected: Approve the number and the role cleanly, one clear action, no paperwork chasing.
got: The offer-review card shows the recommended comp, a band bar placing it within the role salary band, and the rationale, with a single 'Prijmout a odeslat nabidku' button. The hire then surfaces with its questionnaire answers on the Onboarding hand-off tab.
suggested_acceptance: The internal offer approval presents the comp, its band position, and rationale with a single accept action, and the resulting hire appears on the onboarding hand-off tab.
